topics.topic: Exact call-matching semantics for the explicit-None clock trap
questions: Does “with `None`” mean exactly one valid positional argument whose value is `None`, or must the trap also claim otherwise-invalid calls that contain `None`, such as an extra argument or a keyword that the original positional-only function rejects?

Does “with `None`” mean exactly one positional argument whose value is `None`, any call whose time argument binds to `None` including a keyword form, or any argument list containing `None`; and should invalid extra arguments be trapped before CPython reports its ordinary argument error?

quotes:
`time.localtime`, `time.gmtime`, `time.ctime` and `time.asctime` when called
   without an argument or with `None`
judgement.why: Exact wrapper call matching and precedence over Python's ordinary argument validation are implementation-note behavior outside State 4's flow-completeness scope.

topics.topic: State 3 capability used to represent and communicate the explicit-None trigger
questions: Which State 3 capability represents and communicates the new “explicit `None`” trigger to `sandbox_runner`, given that the only argument-sensitive policy capability named there is `SANDBOX_TRAPPED_WITHOUT_ARGUMENT`?

quotes: runner_arguments: [BEHAVIOR] MUST return exactly two arguments: the decimal number launch.channel_fd, the descriptor the program writes every message to, which is the parent's own pipe end inherited at that number; and one JSON text with the members exchange_directory, code_file, inputs (each port, carriage, cardinality and files), output_ports (each name, carriage and cardinality), and memory_bytes, process_count and output_bytes of launch.bounds; its member file_size_limit is the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SANDBOX_SCRATCH_BYTES_MAX constant; its member environment is the imported SANDBOX_ENVIRONMENT constant; its member readable_paths is the imported SANDBOX_RUNTIME_PATHS constant; its member raise_on_call is the imported SANDBOX_TRAPPED_FUNCTIONS constant; its member raise_without_argument is the imported SANDBOX_TRAPPED_WITHOUT_ARGUMENT constant; its member raise_on_every_method is the imported SANDBOX_TRAPPED_CLASS constant; its member raise_unseeded is the imported SANDBOX_UNSEEDED_CONSTRUCTOR constant; its member proc_directory is the imported SANDBOX_PROC_MOUNT constant; the program reads exactly these two arguments after its own path.

runner_source: [BEHAVIOR] The program MUST, before it loads the code, replace every entry point named in raise_on_call with one that raises whatever arguments it is called with, those in raise_without_argument with ones that raise when called without an argument or with None, every method of the class named by raise_on_every_method, and the class named by raise_unseeded when constructed without a seed or with None, and that class's seed method when called on an instance without a seed or with None (A03 rule 4: an explicitly seeded instance draws no entropy and stays usable); and install an audit hook that raises on socket, subprocess and ctypes use and on opening any path outside the exchange directory and the readable_paths.
judgement.why: The later notes explicitly use SANDBOX_TRAPPED_WITHOUT_ARGUMENT as the runner argument and define entries in that list to trap both omitted arguments and explicit None.
